title: Top U.S. Spy Boss Tulsi Gabbard Steps Down for a Heartbreaking Reason
summary: Imagine being the boss of all U.S. spies, but then having to quit because someone you love is very sick. That's what happened to Tulsi Gabbard. She was the Director of National Intelligence—the top spy chief in America. On Friday, she said she was resigning to take care of her husband, Abraham, who was just diagnosed with a super rare bone cancer. "I must step away from public service to be by his side," she wrote. President Trump said she did an "incredible job" and named her deputy, Aaron Lukas, as the acting director. But Gabbard's time in office was unusual. In January, she showed up at an FBI raid on an election office in Georgia! The FBI took ballots and voting machines from the 2020 election. Gabbard said she went because President Trump told her to, and she believed election security was a national security issue. Many people were surprised because spy chiefs don't usually go to FBI raids. Also, last summer, right before the U.S. bombed Iran, Gabbard released a video warning about the dangers of nuclear war. Some officials said she was trying to stop the attack. She had long argued against getting into Middle East wars. Even though she had to leave for a sad reason, some insiders say she might have been pushed out anyway because she didn't always agree with the president's team. Her story shows how even the most powerful jobs can be affected by personal tragedy—and big disagreements over war and peace.
why_it_matters: Even powerful leaders face tough choices between work and family, and disagreements over war and elections can shake up top government jobs, showing that our world’s safety depends on people who sometimes have to put personal life first.

background_read: The Director of National Intelligence oversees America’s spy agencies, like the CIA and NSA, a job created after the 9/11 attacks. The DNI helps the president understand threats to the country.

In 2020, after the presidential election, some people claimed there was cheating, and Georgia became a focus of those disputes. That led to FBI raids on election offices, one of which Gabbard visited.
Last summer, tensions with Iran were high, and some feared a war. Gabbard had long argued against military strikes in the Middle East and spoke out publicly to try to prevent a conflict.

WHY: Her husband’s cancer diagnosis forced her to step away, and her independent views on avoiding wars and questioning election raids made her a target for removal
